Subject: Post-call recap: Private VPC / SOC 2 / vendor SQ — next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Daniel — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

- Priority items we agreed on: SOC 2 attestation details, vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) initiation, and options for Private/VPC or air-gapped deployments for your regulated workloads.
- Action items for FinHealth: share the completed vendor SQ (I'll drop a link below) and confirm any mandatory data residency or encryption requirements beyond HIPAA/GDPR.
- Action items for Redwood: share a short SOC 2 attestation summary, an initial deployment diagram showing VPC/private control plane options, and high-level notes on air-gapped/on-prem capability and timeline.

Attachments I’m sending: Redwood_Private_VPC_Options_v1.pdf (overview of VPC vs on-prem packages) and SOC2_Attestation_Summary_2027.pdf.

For the vendor SQ, you can use this secure form: https://redwood.app.link/vendor-sq?token=abc123 — or if you prefer, attach your spreadsheet and we’ll upload it on our side.

Proposed next step: 30-minute deep-dive with our Solutions Architect (Marissa) to go over network diagrams and HIPAA controls. Here’s our Calendly if you want to pick times: https://calendly.com/redwood/solutions-architect-30min

If you can send the VSQ and your deployment constraints by EOD Thursday (2028-06-15), we can have an initial security readout in next week’s call.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@finhealth.com>

Cc: Arman Patel <arman.patel@finhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private VPC / SOC 2 / vendor SQ — next steps

Thanks Marcus — appreciated the recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- I'll attach our vendor SQ spreadsheet (finhealth_vendor_sq.xlsx) — it has ~120 questions covering SOC/HIPAA/GDPR and network controls.
- SOC 2: we require a current SOC 2 Type II report or attestation. If you can share the high-level attestation summary now we can start internal review; the formal report will be requested later in the procurement process.
- Data residency: for PHI we need a US-only residency option. For other PII we may need EU residency for certain datasets — we’ll flag those if applicable.
- Air-gapped: we are exploring air-gapped on-prem for a narrow set of inference workloads that process unredacted PHI. Please include any constraints and estimated lead times for an air-gapped deployment.

I’ve attached the VSQ. Can Marissa or your solutions architect confirm whether your private deployment supports: 
  1) customer-managed KMS/HSM (we prefer HSM backed keys),
  2) no internet egress from the inference cluster in air-gapped mode,
  3) network diagrams and a list of ports/protocols required for admin/control-plane connectivity.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Daniel
Daniel Wu
Director, IT Security | FinHealth
daniel.wu@finhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-4477

Attachments: finhealth_vendor_sq.xlsx (12 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@finhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Private VPC / SOC 2 / vendor SQ — next steps

Hi Daniel — thanks for sending the VSQ and the clarifying questions. I’m Marissa (Solutions Architect) — looping in details below and attaching an initial deployment diagram. 

Quick answers up front: 
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM: supported. We have integrations with common KMS providers and support HSM-backed key storage for Private deployments (requires onboarding with our infra team).
- Air-gapped / no internet egress: supported for our on-prem package. In air-gapped mode the inference cluster runs entirely in the customer network; admin/control-plane connectivity can be configured over a dedicated management VPN or shipped appliance for offline key injection.
- Ports/protocols: the admin/control-plane needs outbound TLS to our control endpoint for management (can be tunneled over an internal bastion or direct VPN). For fully air-gapped installs we provide an appliance-based control sync process.

I’ve attached: redwood-deployment-diagram.png (initial VPC vs on-prem figure) — it includes: private control plane (customer-managed VPC), optional on-prem appliance, KMS integration points, and network flow for KV cache and model runtime.

HIPAA/GDPR notes: we log access and provide audit trails; PHI must be isolated to dedicated hardware in our Dedicated/Private offering. For EU residency we can pin data planes to EU regions or do an on-prem install in your EU data center if required.

Next steps I suggest: 
- Schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive (Marcus will coordinate).
- We’ll complete the VSQ rows related to SOC 2 attestation and provide the attestation summary PDF for procurement.
- If you confirm air-gapped is required for the PHI path, we’ll prepare an SOW-level estimate for appliance/on-prem lead time (typically 8–12 weeks depending on procurement).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-deployment-diagram.png (1.2 MB)

Daniel
